key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (incidence at least 3%): neutropenia, increased ALT, injection site erythema, upper respiratory infections, and urinary tract infections. In the placebo-controlled population, neutropenia occurred in 7% (150 mg) and 10% (200 mg) vs 0.2% placebo. Most common serious adverse reactions were infections; serious infections that may lead to hospitalization or death are the principal risk (boxed warning).

detail.text: WARNING: RISK OF SERIOUS INFECTIONS. Patients treated with KEVZARA are at increased risk for developing serious infections that may lead to hospitalization or death; opportunistic infections have also been reported.

citations.quote: ## WARNING: RISK OF SERIOUS INFECTIONS

Patients treated with KEVZARA are at increased risk for developing serious infections that may lead to hospitalization or death [see *Warnings and Precautions* (5.1), *Adverse Reactions* (6.1)]. Opportunistic infections have also been reported in patients receiving KEVZARA. Most patients who developed infections were taking concomitant immunosuppressants such as methotrexate or corticosteroids.

summary.text: KEVZARA (sarilumab) received a standard (non-expedited) BLA approval on May 22, 2017 for moderately to severely active RA in DMARD inadequate responders. Efficacy was established in two phase 3 randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials (Study 11072 and Study 10832) with the primary endpoint of ACR20 at Week 24. The original BLA (received October 30, 2015) received a Complete Response action on October 28, 2016 due to manufacturing site issues; Sanofi resubmitted March 22, 2017. No REMS was required, and the application was not referred to an advisory committee because this biologic is not the first in its class.
